updates.note: Reported the partial reopening for Gulfwater as a port-conditions update.

Announced the partial reopening of the ship channel; said traffic would move "in a controlled sequence" and inner-channel vessels remain subject to Unified Command decontamination requirements; gave no date for lifting the restriction.
Wrote the Ledger's partial-reopening story (arc beat), focused on relief cargo stuck in the anchorage backlog.

Called the partial reopening "a turning point for the port and for the region"; said the port is working through the anchorage queue with the Coast Guard one transit at a time; deferred the inner-channel decision to the Coast Guard and Unified Command.

Said Gulf Provider had a berth window and trucks lined up before the channel shut; called the 40 containers "floating inventory" while the ship waits in the anchorage line; promised to release cargo to relief agencies as soon as it is alongside.

Said "partial is the operative word"; warned against modeling a quick return to pre-storm volumes until inner-channel transit capacity under decontamination rules is clear; "You don't flip a switch on a port this size. You work the queue."
Wrote a four-weeks-in feature on how the boil-water notice weighs on households without cars near the bay.

Hauls gallon jugs home on the bus; keeps a pot boiling on the stove; "All day I make sure other people's water is safe. Then I come home and do it again for my own kids." Says she'll believe the notice is over when the city says so; her kids ask every morning whether they can drink from the sink ("Todavía no").

"If you have a car, a water line is an hour of your Saturday. If you don't, it's your whole day, and maybe your shift." Described elderly neighbors carrying cases of water up their steps; called it "a planning problem."
Profiled Huy Nguyen the day after the partial reopening; set up the fishing-closure thread.

Boat survived but season lost; keeps the boat tied up each morning; "The boat payment is due on the first, same as always. The bank doesn't have a closure." Watched pelicans fishing: "Somebody should be." If the closure runs into winter: "Fix what I can fix. Wait on what I can't."
Ran a weekend service checklist: boil-water notice, aid-portal phishing warning naming the lookalike domain, rumor reminders.
"We know how long this has gone on, and we're sorry. The notice stays until the plant is repaired and testing shows the water is safe. Please keep boiling."
Wrote a Port Aransas profile of Bill Hargrove, setting up his view of the jetties.

Profiled rebuilding Hargrove Bait & Tackle near the jetties; Rafael gutted the shop; counts ships from his back step again ("you think, OK, the world didn't end"); tells regulars to ask the state about the fishing closure "and bring me a sandwich"; still selling ice, hooks and tackle from a folding table under the "OPEN-ISH" sign and plans to add live bait before the shelves are done. New detail: a box fan airs out the shop; new shelving leans against a bare wall.
Reported live from the dock as Gulf Provider's containers came off.
On Gulf Provider docking: "It's about a month later than anybody wanted. But it's here, it's moving, and the channel is doing what it's supposed to do."
Said Gulf Provider's berthing showed the partial reopening was doing its job; "We know how much this particular cargo matters to people here."

Arc beat: containers finally land. "Forty boxes, one month, one channel"; called the anchorage "a very expensive parking lot offshore"; would not estimate when all 40 reach destinations; wants a backup route plan "before the first hurricane watch" next season.
Wrote the families' guide to the relief airlift.

Announced the relief airlift for families: "The air station is proud to support the relief effort for our neighbors"; said families may notice larger aircraft and more activity; notices will go out through official channels if base services change.
Explained why the relief airlift runs through NAS Corpus Christi; noted daily schedules were withheld as standard practice.

"Our job is to give the relief effort a safe place to land and unload. The cargo belongs to the agencies doing the work in the community. We're the front porch." Said all flights follow the same airfield procedures; did not release daily schedules.
Reported that stomach illness has eased but the notice remains; included what-to-do guidance.

Said the stomach-illness trend is good "because people have been careful"; warned one lapse (tap water, freezer-tray ice) can restart norovirus in a household; boil, wash hands with soap, clean surfaces.
"A few weeks ago I had people in hallway beds holding buckets. Now the hallway is a hallway again." Urged people to keep boiling.
Feature from Flour Bluff on neighbors watching the relief airlift.

Films the relief airlift from his Flour Bluff street; "These ones have a schedule and a reason. I like that better." Contrasted the airlift with the earlier lights; "This feels like something happening for us."
Reported the pump parts' arrival at O.N. Stevens.

Parts arrived: "This is the day we've been working toward, and I know it's later than anyone wanted." Crews will install and test; notice stays until testing shows the water is safe; gave no date, saying testing "has to be right, not fast."

Apologized for the delay; explained that with her own warehouse under water the company pulled parts from wherever they existed and put them on whatever freight was moving; "Every leg of that trip was slower than normal."
Service explainer: why the notice stays after parts arrive; warned residents that screenshots are not announcements.
"Parts on the dock are not the same as safe water at your tap. We'll lift the notice when the testing says we can, and not an hour before."
Calallen feature on Leticia Ramos' water runs as the city waits for the notice to lift.
Utility won't set a date until parts are installed and testing is complete; "The last thing anyone wants is for us to lift the notice and then have to put it back."

Keeps a list of every household on her Calallen street (who has a car, who needs water dropped off, babies and aging parents); "the list is the only thing that's run on schedule"; frustrated to learn news "from the TV"; "I don't need a promise. I need a date." Plans an ice-and-tap-water block party when the notice lifts.
Weekly roundup: airlift halfway, depot repairs, off-base boil-water reminder.
Thanked families and neighbors for patience with the airlift: "Every one of those aircraft is carrying help for the Coastal Bend."
Depot crews still working through hangar roof damage and water intrusion; "Our workforce has been patient and resilient... We're getting there, step by step."
Broke the AIS identity-anomaly story (arc beat); Gulfwater has not identified the transmitting vessel; no attribution.

Flagged FV Pelican Ridge's identity broadcasting off Port Aransas on the night of Oct. 14-15 while the vessel reported ~600 nm away; "consistent with identity spoofing"; "AIS is a self-report"; declined to say what vessel was transmitting or why; would want radar or imagery before saying more.
Local explainer on the AIS anomaly, crediting Gulfwater's Henrik Aalto with the first report.

Explained spoofing for general readers: "The network trusts the radio"; only radar or satellite imagery can show which hull was really there; "The data only gives you the anomaly. Anything past that is a guess, and I don't guess in public."
Reported the notice lifted after 35 days with post-notice flushing guidance.
Arc beat: notice lifted. "We know what we asked of people: every pot boiled, every case of water carried home... The repairs are done, the testing is done, and the water is safe to drink."

Arc beat: relief as the notice lifts. Heard from a neighbor first; filled a glass at the sink, drank it, then called everybody on her list; asked the city to "tell us sooner what's going on... It's the silence that's hard."
Broke the FAA GPS interference notice; noted neither the FAA nor the Navy would speculate on the source.
"The relief flights are continuing safely... they're flying with backup navigation. No impact to the relief mission."
Arc beat: GPS interference notice. Pilots in the area should be prepared for unreliable GPS signals, use other means of navigation, and report interference to air traffic control.
Sunday feature at Pastor Whitfield's hub after the notice lifted.

Poured her last boiled water on the potted plants by her front door Saturday night and drank tap water "like it was champagne. ¡Por fin!" The place she rents near the bay still has storm damage and she is waiting on her landlord ("The walls, I can't boil").

First Sunday after the notice lifted: line is now about roofs, mold and rent; "Water was the emergency everybody could see. Now we're into the emergencies you can't see from the street." "A container at the port is not a box in somebody's kitchen." Invited planners to "come stand in my hall for one hour."
GPS interference explainer; noted no agency has said whether an investigation is under way; did not speculate on the source.
Aircrews flying into the field are briefed on the notice; "Crews are using backup navigation, which is exactly what they train for."
"Every pilot is trained to navigate without GPS"; ground-based navigation aids, ATC radar and onboard systems keep flights safe; the notice makes sure crews expect it.
Arc beat: station power outage and services update, with practical outage reminders for families.

Arc beat: generator outage statement. "Power is restored, and we're reviewing what happened with the backup generator"; pointed families to official channels; declined to give details during the review.
"Power has been restored. We're reviewing the generator failure and will share what we can when that review is complete." Did not say whether the outage affected the relief airlift.
Wrote a signed opinion column (she kayaks Nueces Bay) calling for a plain-language bay testing/reopening timeline and a way for fishers to document losses now.
Quoted again in Navarro's column: "The bank doesn't have a closure."
North Beach feature on lingering shoreline questions as complaints ease.
Shoreline complaints have come down as cleanup progressed; advice unchanged: avoid oil, wash with soap and water, see a doctor for trouble breathing.

Smelled oil on North Beach two days after landfall ("like a shop with the vents shut"); now "mostly gone isn't gone"; "I'll believe it's clean when somebody shows me the numbers... I'm saying show me." New detail: has started walking the beach again some mornings (staying off the wet sand) while still waiting for an official all-clear; keeps his own count of what the tide leaves.
As the airlift wound down: "We're proud the air station could support this effort for our neighbors"; thanked Flour Bluff and the south side for putting up with the noise.
Marsh feature with Dr. Nathan Brooks six weeks after the spill.

Explained marsh oiling with a sponge analogy; surge lifted oil above normal tide reach and left it in grass and mud; declined to give a recovery date ("A marsh isn't a parking lot... The answer comes in pieces"); declined to discuss how the valves opened ("That's not my field").
Arc beat: first breaking report of the blast at the jetties, filed about two hours after it happened.

Arc beat: channel closure statement. At approximately 1 a.m. the Coast Guard received a report of an explosion near the Port Aransas jetties involving the tug Corrin Bay; two crew injured; channel closed to all vessel traffic until further notice; "The cause is unknown, and we will not speculate."
Co-wrote the Ledger's main blast story; interviewed Hargrove in Port Aransas.
Co-wrote the Ledger's main blast story with Marisol Treviño.
Channel closed to all vessel traffic; priorities are mariner and public safety and care for the injured crew; would not speculate on cause.
Port in close contact with the Coast Guard; "The safety of the people working on the water comes first."

Arc beat: heard the blast at the jetties. It woke him; "I've heard thunder, I've heard tankers lean on their horns at 3 in the morning, and I've heard a hurricane try to move into my shop. This was none of those. One big thump, and then the windows hummed."
Port-conditions update on the closure; noted inner-channel decon restrictions lifted the same day; did not speculate on cause.
Channel stays closed until the Coast Guard determines it is safe for navigation; updates via broadcast notices to mariners; no speculation on cause.
Arc beat: exports stop again after the blast.

Arc beat: second export halt. "Duration is everything. A closure of days is a scheduling problem. A closure of weeks is a supply problem"; called the lifted inner-channel restrictions "a footnote"; "Nobody's pricing a reopening until the Coast Guard says what happened."
Filed the national wire story on the blast; noted the port's strategic-seaport role and the brigade movement postponed before the hurricane; no attribution.
"The channel is closed to all vessel traffic until the Coast Guard determines it is safe. We are not going to speculate about the cause."
"Our focus right now is supporting the Coast Guard and getting accurate information out."
Reported spill cleanup moving to monitoring on the same day as the channel blast.

Arc beat: cleanup phase winds down. Called the move to monitoring "a milestone for the crews"; "Monitoring means we keep checking the shorelines and the marshes... It doesn't mean we're walking away"; keep calling the wildlife hotline; reopening the bays to fishing is a separate decision that depends on testing.
On the monitoring phase: "Monitoring doesn't put shrimp in the boat. Tell me when they test, and tell me what they find."
Evening what-we-know on the blast; cautioned against sharing posts guessing at the cause; reported separately that GPS interference reports stopped.
GPS interference reports have stopped: "We are no longer receiving reports of interference in the area. Pilots should continue to check notices before every flight."
Reported ER visits near normal except bay neighborhoods (+40%) with what-to-do guidance.

Arc beat: lingering visits in low-income tracts. "The overall picture is a recovery story, and that's real. But... the places that took the most surge are still sending noticeably more people to the ER... We want to understand why."
"From triage, you notice the addresses... I can't tell you why from one ER. I can tell you they're still coming." Hallway beds of September are gone.
Special edition after the blast for families; urged readers not to share unit movement details online and to use family readiness groups.
Movement delayed again: "The brigade remains ready to deploy when the port is ready... we'll move when it's safe to move."
Arc beat: what the blast means for the deployment; explained the port-movement chain without disclosing schedules.
"Our soldiers and families have been flexible through two delays now. Readiness doesn't stop because a schedule moves. We'll be ready when the port is ready." No new timeline given.
First interview with the Corrin Bay's captain.

Arc beat: describes the blast. Thirty years running tugs in the channel; "You don't expect the water to come up beside you like that. It went off close, off our port bow. My first thought was my crew. My second thought was my crew." Would not discuss injured crew's conditions ("They did everything right"); would not guess at a cause ("Ask the Coast Guard. I drive tugs"). New detail: tug operated by Laguna Towing.
People-first follow-up on the +40% ER gap in bay neighborhoods; noted officials have not said what drives it.
"Averages can hide a lot... these neighborhoods aren't there yet. We're working through the data to understand what's driving the difference."

Knows the bus route to the nearest hospital "like knowing where the good tacos are"; tells her clients not to wait but watches neighbors wait "because getting anywhere is a whole production... Two buses, a transfer, somebody to watch the kids."
Declined to explain the numbers for the health district: "I can't tell you what the data means. I can tell you what I see... the ER is the only door that's open at 2 in the morning."
Co-wrote the Navy-confirmation story.
Co-wrote the Navy-confirmation story; Port Aransas reaction.
"The channel will reopen when it is safe, and not before."
First statement: "The blast near the jetties was caused by an explosive device"; Navy EOD and mine countermeasures teams searching with the Coast Guard; "We will not discuss the device itself."
"We can confirm the FBI is investigating. We have no further comment at this time."
On the Navy's confirmation: "Folks here are tough... But a storm, you see coming for a week. This, nobody saw coming. That's what's got people rattled."
Port-conditions update on the Navy/Coast Guard search; no speculation on who placed the device.
Vessels at the anchorage should remain clear of the entrance channel and monitor broadcast notices.
"Our teams will search methodically. That takes the time it takes. We will not discuss the device."
Reported exports halted again; traders watching for a prolonged closure.
"Once you hear 'explosive device' and 'search,' you stop modeling days... I'd tell buyers to plan around weeks." "Corpus Christi had a month to recover from one shock. It got two weeks."
Fact-check of the foreign state broadcaster's mockery, with the correction in the headline; declined to name or link the outlet.
"Closing the channel is how you keep people safe while you find out what happened. That's the system working."
Arc beat: mocks the port closure. A segment called it "a harbor America cannot even keep open." Not named or linked by Harborline 6.
Reported the FBI's GPS-transmitter finding; did not name the fuel terminal.

Arc beat: transmitter found. "We can confirm investigators traced the source of the GPS interference to a transmitter located in a parked vehicle... The investigation is ongoing. We're not going to discuss evidence." Did not identify the terminal, the vehicle's owner, or say whether anyone was detained.
"We're glad the reports have stopped, and we thank the pilots who told us what they were seeing."
Good-news edition on the depot's return to full production, plus a weekly safety roundup and Halloween tips.

Arc beat: back to full production. "This is our workforce's day... We couldn't have gotten here without our partners at DLA Distribution Corpus Christi keeping the parts moving." "There's plenty to do, and these are the people who know how to do it."
Explainer on the GPS transmitter finding; stressed what is unknown (who, how long, why, any detentions); no connections drawn.
"The investigation is ongoing. We won't be discussing what was found beyond that."
"Pilots did exactly what they're trained to do. They reported it, and they flew safely."
Halloween feature from Port Aransas as the Navy search continues.

Halloween: folding table and cooler out front, "I'm in the candy business now. Terrible margins." On the blast: "I've lived by these rocks a long time. You learn every sound they make. That one wasn't theirs." New detail: plywood still over one shop window.
Wrote a signed opinion column urging readers not to draw lines between the week's events before officials do, and asking officials for regular scheduled briefings.
